facts.text: BlueboatROSInterface is an rclpy Node that subscribes to /blueboat/cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/Twist) and to the uuv_name-prefixed send_port_motor_0_100_thrust and send_stbd_motor_0_100_thrust topics (std_msgs/Float32), and publishes /blueboat/servo_outputs (std_msgs/Int32MultiArray), /compass (std_msgs/Float32), /imu (sensor_msgs/Imu) and the three Euler-angle Float32 topics.
The node declares uuv_name with default 'blueboat'.
The port and starboard motor callbacks cast the Float32 data to int and call send_motor_thrust with hard-coded motor numbers 3 and 4.
send_motor_thrust sends MAV_CMD_DO_MOTOR_TEST with thrust_type 0 (percent) and duration 1.0 s; its docstring states thrust_value is 0-100 for percent.

arm_vehicle sends MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM with param1 1; disarm_vehicle sends the same command with param1 0. Both methods only call command_long_send and do not read a heartbeat acknowledgement.
send_motor_thrust wraps command_long_send in a try/except whose handler only logs the error.
The constructor initialises self.data to an empty dictionary and starts a daemon MAVLink listener thread.
mavlink_listener stores each received MAVLink message as a dict under its message type in self.data while rclpy.ok() is true.
The node declares mavlink_connection with default udpin:0.0.0.0:14550.
The constructor opens the MAVLink connection and calls wait_heartbeat.
publish_compass reads the VFR_HUD heading, normalises it with heading % 360 and publishes it as a Float32 on /compass.
_publish_servo_outputs reads servo1_raw through servo8_raw from the SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW snapshot, with 0 for a missing field, and publishes them as an Int32MultiArray.
publish_imu reads ATTITUDE roll, pitch and yaw in radians and RAW_IMU linear acceleration, publishes normalised Euler angles as Float32 degrees and builds a sensor_msgs/Imu message.
set_stabilize_mode_and_arm waits for HEARTBEAT messages and checks base_mode & MAV_MODE_FLAG_SAFETY_ARMED; it raises when the vehicle did not arm.
JoystickNode publishes axis 4 and axis 1 times 100 times 0.5 as port and starboard thrust and calls arm_vehicle for button 7 and disarm_vehicle for button 6.
main starts 'ros2 run joy joy_node' with subprocess.Popen before creating the nodes.
changing_modes.py constructs BoatController on udpin:0.0.0.0:14550 and keeps a commented udpin:192.168.2.1:14550 alternative.

determinism.notes: The fake is a stateful Python stand-in; it runs no ROS node, MAVLink connection, Gazebo world or wall-clock timer, so it makes no trajectory or state-hash replay claim.

fidelity.engine: analytic:Python fake of BlueboatROSInterface (no ROS, MAVLink or physics)
gaps: the fake substitutes for the BlueboatROSInterface class only; it starts no ROS 2 node, MAVLink connection, ArduPilot SITL, Gazebo world or sensor
the motor commands are recorded as percentages; the fake integrates no thrust, hydrodynamics, ArduPilot motor test or vehicle motion
the observation values are placeholders and do not come from VFR_HUD, ATTITUDE, RAW_IMU or SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW traffic
the fake's arm and disarm change the stored HEARTBEAT base_mode at once; upstream they only transmit the command, and base_mode changes only if ArduPilot's next HEARTBEAT reports it

the e-stop and the zero-thrust-and-disarm action record the calls; upstream they are transmission-only MAVLink commands (no COMMAND_ACK, heartbeat or motor read-back), so the e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED and nothing proves that ArduPilot disarmed or that the boat stopped
the reads return the node's last stored MAVLink message of each type with no age check, so after a link loss they keep serving stale values; the fake's snapshots never age

live construction is not exercised: BlueboatROSInterface is an rclpy Node (it needs rclpy.init in the host process), waits for a MAVLink heartbeat on udpin:0.0.0.0:14550 without a timeout, arms the vehicle in its constructor and raises when arming fails, and starts a listener thread; a real BlueBoat sending MAVLink to that port would be armed and driven the same way (changing_modes.py keeps a commented 192.168.2.1 endpoint)

the module's main() also starts joy_node and a JoystickNode that publishes -50..50 percent thrust on the same motor topics and arms or disarms from buttons 7 and 6; the 0-100 percent limit follows the send_motor_thrust docstring
the ROS topic wiring, QoS, launch files, MAVLink connection and the ros_ign_bridge topics are outside this in-process fake

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop: the e-stop sends zero motor-test thrust to motors 3 and 4 and a MAVLink disarm through the node, which only transmits them and reads no COMMAND_ACK or heartbeat, so it reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; ArduPilot SITL and Gazebo keep running, a joystick or other MAVLink client can re-arm, and nothing shows that the boat stopped.
